name: Greece
hook: Athens, Olympus and ouzo: the Greek facts behind a thousand classical clues.

facts.label: Athens
facts.statement: Athens, the capital, was called "the eye of Greece"; Paul preached on the Areopagus hill there.

facts.label: Crete
facts.statement: Crete is Greece's largest island; the Ottomans took it in 1669 after a 21-year siege, and Greece gained it in 1913.

facts.label: Macedonia
facts.statement: Philip II of Macedonia conquered Greece in 338 B.C.; when today's North Macedonia became independent in 1991, Greece objected to its name and flag.

facts.label: Mount Olympus
facts.statement: Mount Olympus, on the border of Thessaly and Macedonia, is Greece's highest peak at 9,750 feet.

facts.label: ouzo
facts.statement: Ouzo is the anise-flavored Greek aperitif that turns cloudy when water or ice is added.

facts.label: Lord Byron
facts.statement: Lord Byron died in Greece in 1824 while helping its freedom fighters; most of him was returned to England, but his lungs stayed.

facts.label: Cyprus
facts.statement: Cyprus became independent in 1960 under a settlement among Britain, Greece and Turkey; the two countries nearly went to war over it in 1967 and 1974.
